p:cNvPr.descr: The structures of a few coenzymes containing adenosine. At the top is the structure of coenzyme A. The adenosine is on the far right, shaded orange, bracketed and labeled 3’-phosphoadenosine diphosphate (3’-P-ADP). The adenosine structure consists of 3 rings. The largest ring is the pentose, whose apical O bonds down and left to C, which bonds up to CH2 (5’), down to H (4’), and down and right to C. C bonds up to H and down to O (3’), which bonds down to P. P double bonds left to O, right to O-, and down to O-. C bonds right to C, which bonds up to H and down to OH (2’). C bonds up and right to C, which bonds down to H (1’) and up to N, and up and left to the initial O. The N is part of a 5-sided ring structure. N bonds up to C, which double bonds up and right to N. N bonds down and right to C, which double bonds down to C. C bonds left to the initial N. A 6-sided ring is bonded to the right. Its apical C bonds up to NH2, down and right to N, which bonds down to C. C double bonds down and left to N, which bonds up and left to C. C bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to the initial C. This is the structure of adenosine, and is found on all of the structures in the diagram. The CH2 in the adenosine bonds left to O, which bonds left to 2 consecutive phosphate groups. The left O on the second phosphate group bonds left to CH2, which bonds left to C. C bonds up and down to CH3 and left to C, which bonds up to H, down to OH, and left to C, which double bonds down to O and left to N. N bonds up to H and left to CH2, which bonds left to C. C double bonds down to O and left to N, which bonds up to H and left to CH2. CH2 bonds left to CH2, which bonds left to HS. A bracket extends from this N to the left end of the chain; this is labeled beta-mercaptoethylamine. Everything from the last double bonded O all the way to the right is bracketed and labeled pantothenic acid below. Below, on the left side, is the structure of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+). The adenosine is toward the bottom and is shaded orange. The CH2 on the adenosine bonds left to O, which bonds up to P. P double bonds left to O, right to O-, and up to O. O bonds up to the remainder of another phosphate group. The topmost O bonds right to CH2, which is part of a pentose ring. The apical O bonds down and left to C, which bonds up to CH2, down to H, and down and right to C. C bonds up to H and down to OH. C bonds right to C, which bonds up to H and down to OH. C bonds up and right to C, which bonds down to H, up to N, and up and left to the initial O. N double bonds up and left to C, which bonds up to C, which double bonds up and right to C. C bonds down and right to C, which bonds up to a nicotinamide. C double bonds down to C, which bonds down and left to N. The nicotinamide consists of a C double bonded up to O and right to NH2. To the right is the structure of flavin adenosine dinucleotide (FAD). The CH2 on the adenosine bonds up to the O of a phosphate group, which bonds up to another phosphate group. The top O from the second phosphate group bonds up to CH2, which bonds up to CHOH, bonds up to CHOH, which bonds up to CHOH. CHOH bonds up to CH2, which bonds up to N. The N begins the structure of 3 6-sided rings. This N begins the center ring. It bonds up and right to C, which bonds up to C and double bonds up and left to N. N bonds down and left to C, which bonds down to C, which bonds down and right to N. The ring to the left is a benzene ring with 2 CH3 on 2 of the leftmost carbons. The ring on the right contains an apical double bonded O, which double bonds down to C. C bonds down and right to NH, which bonds down to C. C double bonds down and right to O and down and left to N. N double bonds up and left to C. C bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to the initial C. A brackets on the right side encompasses the molecule from the bottom CH2 to the rings, and is labeled “riboflavin” on the right.
